chunks: Abu 'Ali al-Ash'ari narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

One may perform prayer over the جنازة at any hour, for it is not a prayer involving ruku' or sujud. Rather, only the prayer in which there is khushu', ruku', and sujud is considered disliked at sunrise and at sunset, because it sets between the two horns of Satan and rises between the two horns of a Satan.

key_terms.الْجِنَازَةِ: the deceased person or funeral over whom the prayer is performed
key_terms.الْخُشُوعُ: devotional humility and submissiveness within prayer
key_terms.سُجُودٍ: prostration as an integral act of salat
key_terms.طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ: the rising of the sun, a time associated with dislike for certain prayers
key_terms.قَرْنَيِ الشَّيْطَانِ: the two horns of Satan, an expression linked to the time of sunrise and sunset

ai.seo_question: Can salat over the deceased be performed at sunrise or sunset?
ai.summary: This hadith states that salat over the deceased may be performed at any time, because it is not a prayer that includes ruku' and sujud. The dislike concerning prayer at sunrise and sunset applies to regular salat with bodily acts of devotion, not to the funeral prayer.
